evidence: The hunk shows `if !acquired { return nil }`, so a busy lock does skip the drain; but the lock holder is itself draining the same queue, so the stale-read window is narrow, and PR #37 deleted the queue three days later. The thread has no reply and the PR merged four minutes after review.
guidance_note: When a boundary precondition is made best-effort (skip on busy lock), state in the doc comment why skipping is safe so the reviewer's question is answered in the code.

evidence: The test calls `st.applyMutationQueueLocked(context.Background())` directly, while the PR renamed the suite around DrainMutationQueue; the name/target mismatch is visible in the hunk. No reply, and the PR merged minutes later.
guidance_note: When renaming tests around a new public entry point, make each renamed test call that entry point or keep the helper name in the test name.

narrative: Single Copilot round with two findings on a queue-drain refactor; neither thread got a reply and the PR merged four minutes after the review. The busy-lock finding is real but low-stakes because the lock holder drains the same queue, and the queue was removed outright in PR #37.
guidance_observations: Merging four minutes after review with zero thread replies skipped the address-pr-reviews step entirely, leaving no record of why either finding was dismissed.

evidence: The agent's issue comment says it 'removed all prompt-field wiring from this PR' and filed lit-c5519f81-fd5dbd02, which does not contest that model.Issue lacks Prompt. Removing the half-landed feature and ticketing it is a sound cure for a change set that referenced a nonexistent field.
guidance_note: Run `go build ./... && go test ./...` on the exact branch being pushed before opening the PR; five of thirteen findings here were compile errors on a missing Prompt field.

evidence: The hunk shows `_ = v.Unmarshal(&cfg)`; the issue comment says config loading now hard-fails, and PR #33's copy of Load shows `if err := v.Unmarshal(&cfg); err != nil { return Config{}, fmt.Errorf("decode config: %w", err) }`.
guidance_note: Never write `_ =` on an error from a config parser in new code; return the error from the start.

evidence: 'Field <x> validation failed' was emitted when requiredFieldValue returned !ok, i.e. an unknown config field, not a failed issue; the agent changed the text to 'Field <name> not found'. That change was not carried into the docs PR #33 added, which is what PR #33/F6 caught.
guidance_note: When changing a user-visible message, grep the repo and any stacked branches for the old string and update docs in the same commit.

evidence: The hunk shows the leading `--json` case reduced to `// Consumed and discarded`, so `lit --json <cmd>` lost JSON output. The agent 'removed parseGlobalFlags and restored the prior global output flag flow', which is the reviewer's first option.
guidance_note: Before removing a global flag path, list every behaviour it produced (here: leading --json selects JSON) and keep or explicitly retire each one.

evidence: setupLogging discards the `os.MkdirAll` error and only uses the file `if err == nil`, so a bad log path fails silently. The agent dropped the logging setup from the PR entirely, which removes the silent failure and narrows an over-scoped PR.
guidance_note: Keep a 'derive ready work' PR to that feature; logging setup and global-flag rewrites riding along drew four of the thirteen findings.

evidence: mergeConfigFile has `return nil` on both the not-found branch and the generic error branch, and `_ = v.MergeConfigMap(...)`; PR #33's copy shows mergeConfigFile now returns `([]string, error)` and Load propagates it.
guidance_note: When an error branch and a not-found branch return the same thing, that is the silent-failure bug; distinguish them at write time.

evidence: The test passes `Prompt: "present"` to store.CreateIssueInput, which the agent did not dispute; it removed prompt wiring including test paths.
guidance_note: Run the full test suite on the pushed branch before opening the PR.

evidence: deriveNotReadyReason calls `st.GetIssueDetail(ctx, issue.ID)` per issue, a visible N+1. The issue comment lists seven changes and none touches this; the same finding came back as PR #33/F1 and F2, where it was deferred again.
guidance_note: When a readiness check needs only blocker status, write the bulk store query (open blockers for a set of ids) instead of reusing a full-detail per-item getter.

evidence: The reviewer asked for one shared normalizer; the agent 'removed required-field normalization' from both places. PR #33's Load does a raw `append(globalRequired, projectRequired...)` and PR #33/F3 flagged the missing trim/lowercase/dedupe, which the agent then re-added as normalizeFields.
guidance_note: When told two copies of logic duplicate each other, delete one copy and route both callers through the other; deleting both drops the behaviour.

evidence: requiredFieldValue's `case "prompt": return issue.Prompt` referenced a nonexistent field; the agent removed prompt and also 'removed explicit supported-field mapping', replacing it with JSON marshal/unmarshal (issueFieldValues in PR #33). Removing prompt was right, but the replacement introduced the omitempty defect caught in PR #33/F7 and PR #34/F1.
guidance_note: When replacing an explicit field switch with a generic derivation, check what the derivation drops: JSON marshaling drops every omitempty field.

evidence: Run() switched to parseGlobalFlags and dropped the output-mode helpers that, per the reviewer, error_output.go and output_mode_test.go still referenced; the agent restored the prior output flow, which resolves the dangling references.
guidance_note: Build the whole module before pushing a change that deletes exported-in-package helpers.

evidence: `Prompt: *prompt` in CreateIssueInput; the agent removed the prompt flag wiring and ticketed prompt support, consistent with the reviewer's second option.
guidance_note: Run the build on the pushed branch before opening the PR.

evidence: `update.Prompt = &value` on UpdateIssueInput, same missing field; removed with the rest of the prompt wiring.
guidance_note: Run the build on the pushed branch before opening the PR.

narrative: One Copilot round with thirteen findings, five of them compile errors on a Prompt field the model did not have, plus a dangling reference to deleted output-mode helpers; the PR was pushed without building. The agent answered in one issue comment rather than per thread, cutting prompt, logging, and the global-flag rewrite. Two of its fixes cost later: deleting both normalizers (F9) came back as PR #33/F3, and replacing the explicit field switch with JSON marshaling (F10) produced the omitempty defect in PR #33/F7 and PR #34/F1. The N+1 (F8) went unanswered and resurfaced in PR #33.
guidance_observations: Answering thirteen threads with one issue comment left F8 with no recorded decision, and it was raised again in the next PR.
The PR bundled config loading, logging, global-flag parsing and a prompt field into a 'ready work' change; most findings landed on the unrelated parts.

evidence: The hunk shows `update` dropped from the fish list along with `beads`. The F1 reply says the rebased list 'already includes update', while the F2 reply on the identical bash issue says the agent 'Added update back'; the packet does not settle which is true.
guidance_note: Rebase on master before opening a PR that edits command lists, so a stale base does not silently delete commands added since.

evidence: The bash `commands` string lost `update` while `lit update` is still registered; the agent restored it and added TestCompletionScriptsIncludeUpdateCommand across bash/zsh/fish.
guidance_note: Derive completion command lists from the registered command table, or test them against it, instead of hand-maintaining three strings.

evidence: The hunk calls importBeadsData inside the apply branch before backup creation, so a later backup failure leaves a mutated database; the agent moved the backup ahead of the import.
guidance_note: In any apply path, order the steps so the backup or snapshot precedes the first mutation.

narrative: One round, three findings, all correct and all fixed. Two were the same missing `update` entry in completion lists, apparently a stale-base artifact; the agent's two replies disagree on whether the rebase or its own edit restored it. The import-before-backup ordering fix was a real data-safety fix.
guidance_observations: The two completion replies give contradictory accounts of the same fix; one accurate reply per fix keeps the record trustworthy.

evidence: The hunk sets `Limit: 0` and then derives readiness per issue, so --limit no longer bounds work. The owner replied 'This is terrible. Will rewrite completely' and the agent deferred; PR #34 rewrote ready the next day. Deferral out of a rename PR is defensible, but no ticket id was given and this same cost was already flagged as PR #31/F8.
guidance_note: When deferring a finding, name the ticket id in the reply so it does not resurface unanswered in the next PR.

evidence: Same per-issue `st.GetIssueDetail` N+1 that PR #31/F8 raised and that went unanswered there; here it was acknowledged and deferred alongside F1. It is a repeat of an unaddressed finding, not a consequence of a fix.
guidance_note: Answer every thread in the PR where it is first raised; PR #31/F8's silence is why this came back twice.

evidence: This PR carries PR #31's fixed config code: Load does `cfg.Ready.RequiredFields = mergedRequired` with no trim/lowercase/dedupe because the PR #31/F9 fix deleted both normalizers. The agent re-added normalization as normalizeFields in f5f2c31.
guidance_note: When resolving a duplication finding, keep one copy and route both callers to it rather than deleting both.

evidence: `GOBIN="${GOBIN:-$(go env GOPATH)/bin}"` breaks on a colon-separated GOPATH; the agent switched to `go env GOBIN` with a first-GOPATH-entry fallback.
guidance_note: Ask the toolchain for the install dir (`go env GOBIN`) rather than reconstructing it from GOPATH.

evidence: The new doc says 'Output defaults to plain text', but the reviewer notes --output, LNKS_OUTPUT and non-TTY auto-JSON still exist (and PR #31/F4's fix restored that flow). The agent documented the real precedence; the owner noted --output should eventually be removed.
guidance_note: Write docs from the code's current behaviour, not from the intended end state.

evidence: The added doc lists 'Field <name> validation failed' and a `required_fields = ["prompt"]` example, but the PR #31 fixes renamed that reason to 'not found' and removed the prompt field; the doc was written against pre-fix code. Fixed in f5f2c31.
guidance_note: After a review fix changes a message or removes a field, grep for the old string and field name before writing docs on top of that branch.

evidence: issueFieldValues JSON-marshals the issue, so omitempty fields disappear and read as 'not found' instead of 'not set'; this replaced PR #31's explicit field switch. The reply argues only the performance half ('zero-maintenance field coverage') and never answers the semantic half, which came back as PR #34/F1.
guidance_note: When a finding raises two problems, answer both; a pushback that addresses only the cheaper one leaves the defect in place.

evidence: The README replaced the auto/--output/LIT_OUTPUT description with 'Output defaults to plain text', which the code does not do; the agent restored a description of the auto behaviour and overrides.
guidance_note: Write docs from the code's current behaviour, not from the intended end state.

narrative: A rename PR stacked on PR #31's fixed branch, so most findings landed on PR #31's ready/config code. Three trace to PR #31 fixes: F3 to deleting both normalizers, F6 to doc text written against pre-fix messages, and F7 to the JSON-marshal field derivation. F1 and F2 repeat PR #31/F8's N+1, deferred here without a ticket. The agent pushed back on F7 by answering only its performance half, and the omitempty defect resurfaced in PR #34.
guidance_observations: Stacking a rename on top of an unmerged feature branch carried that branch's open defects into a second review, where they were billed again.
Two replies on F1 and F8 are short owner notes ('This is terrible', '--output should have been removed') followed by agent replies; the owner's direction on --output was not ticketed in the thread.

evidence: newFieldAnnotator validates against `issueFieldValues(model.Issue{})`, a JSON marshal of a zero value, so omitempty fields like assignee read as nonexistent; this is the semantic defect PR #33/F7 raised and the agent dismissed, stemming from the JSON-marshal derivation introduced by the PR #31/F10 fix. The thread is outdated and resolved, but no reply records what changed.
guidance_note: Derive a struct's valid field set from its type (reflect over json tags) rather than from marshaling a zero value.

evidence: The --json shape does change from `{ready, not_ready}` to a flat annotated list, but that wrapper only existed since PR #31 two days earlier in a pre-release tool, so the compatibility concern is overstated. No reply records that reasoning.
guidance_note: When intentionally changing a JSON output shape, say so in the PR description so the compatibility question is answered before review.

evidence: The comment says the unexported key 'prevents construction outside this package', yet `Kind{}` is constructible anywhere and `UnmarshalJSON` does `json.Unmarshal(data, &k.key)` with no registry check. Outdated, but no reply.
guidance_note: When a comment claims a type is a closed set, make every constructor including UnmarshalJSON reject values outside the registry.

evidence: The tests cover `description` and an invalid field but no omitempty field, which is exactly the case F1 shows is broken. No reply.
guidance_note: When validation is derived from a serialization, test at least one field that serialization treats specially (omitempty).

narrative: One round, four findings, no replies on any thread. F1 and F4 are the omitempty defect from the JSON-marshal field derivation that PR #31's fix introduced and PR #33/F7's pushback left in place. F3 is a closed-set comment the code does not enforce; F2 overstates a compatibility concern on a two-day-old output shape.
guidance_observations: A defect dismissed with a partial pushback in one PR (PR #33/F7) cost two more findings in the next one.

evidence: `go-version: "1.25.x"` duplicates the version go.mod already states; `go-version-file: go.mod` keeps one source. The thread is outdated after four commits, but no reply says what changed.
guidance_note: Point CI's toolchain at go.mod instead of restating the version.

evidence: The workflow sets no `permissions` block for a build-and-test job that only needs read access. No reply.
guidance_note: Start every new workflow with `permissions: contents: read`.

evidence: The workflow uses `actions/setup-go@v5`, whose module caching is on by default (since v4), so adding `cache: true` changes nothing. No reply.

The reviewer cites specific call sites (`exec.CommandContext(ctx, "dolt", ...)` in doltcli, `doltcli.Run` in store_test.go), but the packet shows neither the code nor the CI result, so whether a fresh runner fails is unverified. Either way the thread got no reply.
guidance_note: Watch the first CI run of a new workflow go green before merging it.

narrative: A new CI workflow; four findings, no replies, merged two minutes after review. Version duplication and missing permissions are real minor issues; the caching suggestion is wrong for setup-go v5; the missing-Dolt claim cannot be checked from the packet.
guidance_observations: Merging two minutes after review with no replies left no record of which findings were addressed in the four commits.

evidence: The hunk replaces syncDoltRemotesFromGit with `store.OpenSync`, and OpenSync (F3 hunk) goes straight to openStoreConnection with no EnsureDatabase. A first-ever sync in an uninitialized workspace is a real gap, but sync normally runs after init; the packet does not show whether openStoreConnection fails on a missing DB.
guidance_note: When adding a second open path beside Open, list what Open guarantees (EnsureDatabase) and decide explicitly whether the new path needs it.

evidence: SyncFetch trims `remote` but never rejects empty before `DOLT_FETCH`; the outcome is a confusing Dolt error rather than corruption, and CLI callers may already validate, which the packet does not show.
guidance_note: Validate store-method arguments once at the store boundary, the same way OpenSync validates its own.

evidence: Same root as F1: OpenSync validates args and version then calls openStoreConnection with no EnsureDatabase, unlike Open per the reviewer. Whether that fails in practice is not shown.
guidance_note: When adding a second open path beside Open, list what Open guarantees and decide explicitly whether the new path needs it.

evidence: SyncAddRemote passes raw `name, url` to `DOLT_REMOTE add` while formatting the error with `strings.TrimSpace(name)`, so it trims only for messages; inconsistent with SyncFetch. Outdated, no reply.
guidance_note: Normalize each input once at entry and use the normalized value for both the call and the error message.

evidence: SyncRemoveRemote passes the raw `name` to `DOLT_REMOTE remove`, same pattern as F4. Outdated, no reply.
guidance_note: Normalize each input once at entry and use the normalized value for both the call and the error message.

evidence: The hunk confirms `dolt_remotes` now holds `syncState.doltRemotes` from the new store path, but the text callback's `[]map[string]string` assertion is not in the packet, so whether it panics or silently prints nothing is unverified. A potential runtime panic got no reply and the thread is not outdated.
guidance_note: When changing the type behind a `map[string]any` payload key, grep for every type assertion on that key, or pass typed structs instead of `map[string]any`.

narrative: Embedded Dolt sync; six findings, none answered. Two flag OpenSync skipping EnsureDatabase, three flag inconsistent input normalization in the sync store methods, and one flags a possible type-assertion panic after the payload type changed. The panic claim is the most serious and the packet cannot confirm it.
guidance_observations: A possible runtime panic (F6) was resolved with no reply and no visible change, which is the case where a recorded answer matters most.

evidence: hasTruthyBoolFlag matches only `--repair` and returns on the first hit, while Go's flag package accepts `-repair` and lets later flags win, so `lnks fsck -repair` routes a mutating command down the read path. Outdated, no reply.
guidance_note: Classify a command's access mode from the same FlagSet the command parses, not from a hand-rolled matcher that mirrors it.

narrative: One finding: a hand-rolled flag scanner that disagrees with Go's flag parsing and can send a mutating fsck down the read-only path. It was correct and went unanswered; the thread is outdated, so the code may have changed.

evidence: The report maps `managedAssetStatus(hookResult.Changed, false)`, so an up-to-date hook and a hook skipped as incompatible both read 'unchanged', per the reviewer's account of installHooks. Outdated, no reply.
guidance_note: When reporting a writer's result, carry each distinct decision branch (wrote, unchanged, skipped) into the report rather than collapsing to a boolean.

evidence: The install doc hard-codes `/opt/homebrew/opt/icu4c@78/include`, which is wrong on Intel Macs (/usr/local) and custom prefixes; `$(brew --prefix icu4c@78)` is portable. Outdated, no reply.
guidance_note: Use `$(brew --prefix <formula>)` in documented Homebrew paths instead of the local machine's prefix.

evidence: Same hard-coded `/opt/homebrew` prefix in troubleshooting.md, a second copy of the F2 block. Outdated, no reply.
guidance_note: Write a setup snippet once and link to it rather than pasting it into two docs.

narrative: Three findings, no replies: a refresh report that collapses 'skipped' into 'unchanged', and the same hard-coded Homebrew prefix in two docs. All three are correct; the threads went outdated, so fixes may have landed without being recorded.
guidance_observations: The same command block pasted into two docs drew two findings for one problem.
